name: Chicken Xacuti
subtitle: dark roasted-coconut curry heavy with whole spice, the Goan Catholic Sunday chicken

ingredients.note: frozen grated works; desiccated does not
the spice that makes xacuti smell like xacuti
dagad phool, for the earthy back note

prepNotes: Marinate the chicken with the turmeric, half the ginger-garlic paste and salt for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Soak the tamarind in 3 tbsp hot water and squeeze out the pulp before you start; you will want it at the end.
Grate the coconut fresh if you possibly can. The whole dish is built on the flavour of coconut browned in a dry pan.

steps.text: Dry-roast the coconut in a kadhai over low heat, stirring constantly, 10-12 minutes until it is the colour of milk chocolate. Tip it out onto a plate.
steps.tip: Low heat and never stop stirring. Coconut goes from golden to burnt in under a minute, and burnt coconut cannot be rescued.

steps.text: In the same pan roast the chillies, coriander powder, cumin, poppy seeds, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, star anise, mace and stone flower for 2 minutes until fragrant.
steps.tip: Add the coriander powder last. Ground spice scorches far faster than whole seed.

steps.text: Grind the roasted coconut and spices with the nutmeg and about 200ml warm water to a very smooth, thick paste. Give it a full 3-4 minutes in the blender.
steps.tip: Any grittiness left now stays gritty in the finished curry.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil and fry the sliced onion 12 minutes until deep gold and collapsing.
Add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and fry 2 minutes until the raw smell lifts.
Add the marinated chicken and turn it over high heat 6-8 minutes until the pieces are sealed and no longer pink outside.
Stir in the ground masala and cook it down 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and oil beads at the edges.
steps.tip: This is where xacuti gets its depth. If it catches, add a splash of water rather than lowering the flame.

steps.text: Pour in 400ml hot water, season with salt, cover and simmer 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy coats a spoon.
Stir in the tamarind pulp, simmer 3 minutes more, and taste for salt and sourness. Finish with coriander leaves.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and is better on day two once the roasted coconut settles. Reheat gently with a splash of hot water; freezes 2 months.
